name: Bluish steel blue
lede: Bluish Steel Blue is ColorHub's name for Sora-iro (空色), a traditional Japanese color whose name simply means "sky color."

sections.title: Sora-iro, the color of sky
sections.body:
The Wikipedia survey "Traditional colors of Japan" lists this color under the romanized name Sora-iro, written 空色 [1]. The kanji are the plain words for "sky" and "color," and the library's gloss reads "sky blue color" without further embellishment [1]. No book consulted for this project independently dates the name, so any claim beyond that gloss would be invented [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[beaucaire]], [[dusty-steel-blue]], [[dirty-blue]] and [[harbor-blue]], at 3.9, 4.6, 4.9 and 4.9 ΔE [1]. The hex given here, #4D8FAC, is a modern screen approximation chosen to match the gloss, not a measurement of any dyed or painted object [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
A color within range of this swatch appears in 97 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.41 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 43 [2]. That is rarer than 52 percent of the named colors we track [2].

It peaks twice: in paintings dated to the 1900s, at 2.8 times the expected rate, and again in the decade 1910, at 3.6 times the rate for that decade alone [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, in 30 percent of the paintings that carry it [2]. It is also over-represented in French paintings, at 2.5 times the expected rate across 3,443 French works in the archive [2]. The earliest dated appearance we have is Marco Zoppo, 1467, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a true first sighting [2].

origin.named_after: sky color, from 空 (sky) and 色 (color)
origin.first_recorded: undocumented beyond its listing in Japan's traditional color system
